que: que — that, who, which; for · also por que — because, since (= porque) · por que — by which, whereby (por que más valdrá 'whereby he will be worth more') · also que — 'so that, lest' introducing purpose/result (que por miedo non dexen nada; por tal lo faze … que no lo ventasse nadi); after después/mientra 'after, while' (después que, mientra que)
en: en — in, into, on · en — of it, thence (= ende; por en avemos qué fablar 'of which we have to speak') · also en — 'as' (en paria 'as tribute'); en essora 'at that moment' · also en — 'among' (en todos los sos 'among all his men')
buena: bueno — good (fem.); en buen(a) '(born/girded) in a good hour' — the poem's honorific formula
çinxo: çeñir — he girded (strong preterite 3rd sg.; Latin cinxit)
aquel: aquel — that one, whoever · also aquel — that (demonstrative adjective; aquel día de cras 'tomorrow'; aquella mayor az 'that biggest line')
poyo: poyo — hill, rising ground, knoll (Latin podium; poyo que es sobre Mont Real 'the hill above Monreal'; = poyo, closest cerro, colina)
él: él — he (stressed subject pronoun) · also él — 'him, it' after a preposition, of a thing (a él vino; en él fincaredes 'in it', i.e. in Castejón)
priso: prender — he took (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = prendió, tomó)
mientra: mientra — while, as long as (= mientras)
sea: seer — may be, that is (present subjunctive 3rd sg.)
el: el — the (masc.) · also el — 'he who' before a relative (el qui quisiere, el que es sobre Fenares); el before a fem. noun beginning with a vowel (el espada = la espada; el algara = la algara) · also el de + place name 'he of, the one from' (mio Çid el de Bivar)
de: de — of, from · also de — by (the agent with a passive participle; = por) · also de — 'by (night)' (de noch), partitive 'of, among' (quinze moros … de los que alcançava; pocas de gentes), 'as' (de ganançia 'as booty'), 'from outside' (de fuera), 'on the right' (de diestro) · also 'about, concerning' (de mí non digan mal 'let them not speak ill of me') · also de — 'as if in' (commo de arrancada 'as if in rout'); 'in the manner of' (de guisa 'in such a way'); 'of, among' (de bivos pocos 'of the living few'); nominalized infinitive (del prender 'of the taking') · also de — 'with' of manner (de fuertes coraçones 'with stout hearts'); 'on' (de pie 'on foot'); 'from' of side (della e della part 'from both sides'); de cabo 'anew' (de + cabo, 'again'); de suso de 'above'; seños … de seños colpes 'with one blow each' · also de — 'in respect of' after an adjective (sobejana de mala 'exceedingly bad'); 'with regard to, about' (me plaze de mio Çid 'I am pleased about the Cid'); 'from, at the hand of' (de señor non ha graçia 'he gets no favor from a lord'); 'from' of origin (de moros fo 'it came from Moors'); 'at' of manner (de vagar 'at leisure', de + the noun vagar)
moros: moro — Moor (masc. pl.); a moros nin a cristianos, 'to any living soul' (merism)
e: e — and (= modern y) · also aver — I have (1st sg. present, apocopated form of he, perfect auxiliary: Espeso e el oro, 'I have spent the gold')
la: el/la — the (fem.); her/it (object pronoun) · also la que 'the one that' (Çelfa la que dizen de Canal 'Çelfa, the one they call of the Canal')
mio: mio — my (unstressed possessive; mio Çid 'my lord Cid')
çid: Çid — the Cid, 'lord' (Arabic sīdī 'my lord'; pronounced Tsid)
por: por — through, along, by, for · purpose, 'in order to' (por el reyno quitar 'to quit the kingdom'); por + inf. 'yet to be done' (tres an por troçir 'three remain to pass'); 'for, on behalf of' (por mio Çid) · also por — 'out of, because of' (por miedo 'through fear'); 'for (that reason)' (por tal lo faze 'he does it for that reason'); 'by way of' (por Guadalfajara); por + noun 'for the sake of' ; por coraçón 'willingly' · also 'for (a price)' (por quanto serié conprada 'for how much it would be bought'); 'by means of' (por carta 'by writ'); 'through, thanks to' (por mí ganaredes 'through me you will gain') · also por — 'on, during (a time)' (por aquesta mañana 'this morning'); 'by way of, through' (por medio de la llaña 'through the middle of the plain')
carta: carta — letter, written decree · also 'written deed, charter' (escripta es la carta 'the charter (of peace) is written'; por carta 'in writing')
estando: estar — being, standing (gerund; estando en la cruz 'while on the cross'; = estando)
tierra: tierra — land, country; one's own land · earth (fezist çielo e tierra 'you made heaven and earth'; por tierra 'on earth')
val: valer — help! (imperative 2nd sg., apocopated for vale; = vale)
martín: Martín (Antolínez) — a knight of Burgos, companion of the Cid, who provisions him on his exile and negotiates the loan from Raquel and Vidas
todo: todo — all, every (de todo conducho, 'with every kind of provision')
lo: lo — him, it (object pronoun) · lo que perdedes 'that which you lose' (neuter antecedent of the relative) · also lo — neuter article 'what is' (lo to 'what is yours'); pleonastic 'it' (lo an, lo han a far; por tal lo faze 'for that reason he does it')
metió: meter — he put (preterite 3rd sg.; metió mano 'laid hand to'; = metió)
paria: paria — tribute paid by a Muslim town for protection (sg.; en paria 'as tribute'; see parias)
a: a — to, at · also aver — he/she has (3rd sg. present, h-less spelling of ha, as in el rey me a ayrado = el rey me ha airado) · personal a before a direct object (salvest a Jonás; a ti adoro); a + inf. 'to, about to' (tornólas a catar); a tan grand sabor 'with so great pleasure'; a ojo 'in plain sight' · also a — 'into' (sacar a çelada 'to lure into ambush'); 'at, in' (a la çaga 'at the rear'); 'against' (dar salto a la çaga); dative 'to' (a mí dedes); haber a + inf. 'have to' (lo han a far); a + noun of direction (adeliñava a la puerta 'made for the gate') · impersonal 'there is' (aver; es dia a de plazo 'there is (only) a day of the term', the most likely reading of a hard line); ha as auxiliary set after the participle (soñado a 'he has dreamt') · also 'on, at (a time)' (a tercer dia 'on the third day') · also a — 'has' before the participle, agreeing with the object (la lança a quebrada 'he has broken the lance'; a menester 'has need of'); a + dative of the person affected (a Minaya matáronle el cavallo 'they killed Minaya's horse')
plaze: plazer — it pleases (present 3rd sg., impersonal; non plaze 'it does not please, they dislike it'; = place)
los: el — the (masc. pl.); them (object pronoun) · also los que 'those who' (demonstrative use before a relative); los — him, them as object of consejar (commo los consejava 'as he advised them') · also los de 'those of' (con los de Castejón 'with the men of Castejón')
firme: firme — firm; used adverbially, 'firmly, securely' (= firmemente) · also firme' — firmes, 'firm, steadfast' (adjective plural, final s dropped; firme' son los moros 'the Moors are firm', i.e. still holding their ground)
mientre: mientre — adverb-forming suffix, 'in a manner' (Latin mente; fuerte mientre = fuertemente)
pesava: pesar — it grieved, it weighed on (imperfect 3rd sg.; les pesava 'it grieved them'; = pesaba)
vío: veer — he saw (strong preterite of veer 'to see'; = vio, here two syllables ví-o)
caboso: caboso — accomplished, excellent (adj., also used alone as a noun, 'the excellent one')
minaya: Minaya — the title by which the Cid's kinsman Álvar Fáñez is called, usually explained as mi + anaya 'my brother'
yentes: yente — people, folk (= gente; y- from Latin g-)
fizo: fazer — he made, did, caused (strong preterite 3rd sg.; fizo posar 'he made (them) halt'; = hizo)
teruel: Teruel — Teruel, city in Aragon (= Teruel)
don: don — don, lord (honorific title) · also don — gift (noun; en don 'as a gift') · also don — from where, whence (= donde, de onde; Castejón don abremos grand enpara 'Castejón, from which we shall have great protection')
rodrigo: Rodrigo — Rodrigo, the Cid's given name (= Rodrigo)
roy: Roy — Ruy, short for Rodrigo (Roy Díaz = Rodrigo Díaz, the Cid)
las: el/la — the (fem. pl.); them (fem. object pronoun)
ovo: aver — he had (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = hubo; here perfect auxiliary, ovo bastidos = 'he had furnished') · ovo de + inf., little more than a plain past (las manos se ovo de untar 'his hands were smeared'); dont a ojo los ovo 'as soon as he had them in sight'
cabo: cabo — beside, next to (preposition; cf. modern cabe) · also cabo — end (noun; fasta cabo del año, 'until the end of the year') · also de cabo — 'again, anew' (que los cometamos de cabo 'that we attack them again'; = de nuevo) · also a cabo de — at the end of, after (a cabo de tres sedmanas 'after three weeks')
venido: venir — come (past part.; venido es 'has come', ser as perfect auxiliary; = venido)
es: seer — it is (present 3rd sg.) · also ser as perfect auxiliary of intransitives (exido es 'has gone out') and passive auxiliary (la tienda es cogida)
son: seer — they are (3rd pl.) · also son — perfect auxiliary of intransitives and passive auxiliary (todos son exidos 'have all gone out'; nombrados son; son derramadas 'are scattered')
sabet: saber — know, mark you (imperative 2nd pl., sabed; sabet = sabed; epic tag addressed to the audience)
peonadas: peonada — company of foot-soldiers (collective from peón; = peonada, which in modern Spanish means a group of laborers or a day's labor)
vido: veer — he saw (strong preterite 3rd sg.; Pidal's vi[d]o; = vio)
sin: sin — without · also sin — 'besides, apart from' (sin las peonadas 'besides the foot-soldiers'); sin falla 'without fail'; sin dubda
falla: falla — failure, lack (noun; sin falla 'without fail'; = falla, closest falta)
besóle: besar + le — he kissed his (besó 3rd sg. preterite + dative le 'his', the accent written on the verb's stressed vowel; besóle las manos 'he kissed his hands'; = le besó)
gelo: ge + lo — it to him/them (ge, ancestor of modern se, + lo; = se lo)
dize: dezir — he says (present 3rd sg.; Dize Minaya 'Minaya says'; = dice)
nada: nada — nothing; por nada 'for anything (in the world)'
campeador: Campeador — the Battler, the Champion (the Cid's epithet, from campo 'field of battle')
fermoso: fermoso — beautiful (f- for h-; = hermoso) · also fermoso — as adverb 'warmly, graciously' (fermoso sonrrisava 'he smiled warmly')
sonrrisava: sonrrisar — he was smiling (imperfect 3rd sg.; fermoso sonrrisava 'he smiled warmly'; = sonreía)
grado: grado — thanks (grado a … 'thanks be to …') · also grado — will, good will (de grado 'willingly, gladly'; de grado non avrié nada, 'of good will there would be nothing to be had')
dios: Dios — God · also Dios! — interjection of wonder (Dios, cómmo se alabavan! 'God, how they boasted!')
vertudes: vertud — power, virtue (= virtud; sus vertudes santas 'his holy powers')
vos: vos — you (object pronoun, polite/plural) · also subject 'you' (vos, que por mí dexades 'you who leave for my sake'); dative 'to you' (dar vos quiero vuestra part) · also reflexive/ethic 'you (yourselves)' (id vos en algara 'go off on a raid'); dative with an impersonal sense (si cueta vos fore 'if need befall you')
visquiéredes: bivir — you shall live (future subjunctive 2nd pl., strong stem visqu- from Latin vixerit; mientra que visquiéredes 'as long as you live'; = viviereis, a tense now obsolete)
bien: bien — well · bien — good, benefit (noun; algún bien vos pueda far 'some good I may do you') · bien — very, quite, intensifying an adverb (bien çerca del agua 'very near the water')
me: me — me, to me · also reflexive 'myself' (fata que yo me pague 'until I am satisfied')
irá: ir — it will go (future 3rd sg.; irá a mal 'will go to ruin'; = irá)
fo: seer (and ir, which shares this preterite) — he/it was; went (preterite 3rd sg.; = fue, restored by Pidal as f[o]; of this part's three occurrences, fo entrado and fo acusado are periphrastic/passive ser + past part. constructions, while fo algo is a plain copula with a pronoun predicate, 'was something') · also commo fo tu voluntad, ca fo tu voluntad 'as/for it was your will' (ser + noun subject, 'it was'; Pidal restores f[o]) · also se fo acomendar 'went to commend himself' (ir); fo de noch 'it was night' (ser de + noun, 'night had come'); fo desenparada (passive, 'was abandoned') · also fo — went (ir; mañanas fo Minaya 'in the morning Minaya went'); fo de moros 'it came from the Moors' (ser de + noun of origin; Pidal restores f[o])
fonssado: fonssado — army, host (Latin fossatum 'ditch, entrenched camp'; in medieval Castile also a military expedition and the service owed for it; rancar el fonssado, Pidal 'vencer al ejército'; = hueste, ejército)
era: seer — it was (imperfect of seer = ser)
compañas: compaña — company, band of troops (pl.; = compañas, closest tropas)
aquellas: aquel — those (fem. pl.; here referring back to the chests)
dexado: dexar — left, left behind (past part.; = dejado)
álbar: Álbar — Álvar (personal name, Álbar Fáñez; = Álvar)
pagó: pagar — he paid, rewarded (preterite 3rd sg.; qué bien pagó a todos sus vassallos 'how well he paid all his vassals'; = pagó)
quel: que + le — who ... him (que + enclitic/elided le) · that ... to him (quel creçe conpaña 'that company grows for him')
dixo: dezir — he/she said (strong preterite; x = sh-sound; = dijo)
pagado: pagar — satisfied, pleased; also paid (past part.; será pagado = 'he will be content with')
ya: ya — O! (vocative particle, Arabic yā); also 'now, already' · also ya — 'would', reduced imperfect of aver as conditional ending, 3rd sg., after infinitive + clitic (pagar se ya 'would be satisfied'; = -ía)
más: más — more; e más 'and moreover' · non más 'no more, nothing more'; por que más valdrá 'whereby he will be worth more'
nos: nos — we (subject pronoun; = nosotros) · also nos — us, to us (object pronoun; atorgar nos hedes 'you will grant us') · also reflexive 'ourselves' (nos partimos 'we part'); dative (la missa nos dirá 'will say for us') · also nos' — non + se (aun nos' van del campo 'they are still not leaving the field'; the apostrophe marks the elision)
ora: hora — hour (= hora); en buen ora, part of the poem's honorific birth-formula, 'born in a good hour' · al ora 'at that very hour, then' (en ti crovo al ora)
nasco: nacer — he was born (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = nació)
mano: mano — hand (sg.); en vuestra mano = 'in your keeping'
noch: noche — night (apocopated form of noche; cf. anoch)
d: de — of, with (elided form of de before a vowel, d'arena = de arena) · de — from (unos d'otros 'one from another')
va: ir — he/she goes (present 3rd sg.; = va); ir + gerund, 'to be (gradually) doing' · ir + infinitive 'goes to' (la manol va besar 'goes to kiss his hand', el Duero va passar 'goes to cross the Duero') · also va — 'there is, goes on' impersonal (¡Qué priessa va en los moros! 'what a stir there is among the Moors!')
al: a + el — to the; al menos 'even the least' · also a + el standing for a + la before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel (al espada = a la espada) · also al — 'other thing, the rest' (neuter, Latin alius; de lo al non pienssan nada 'of anything else they think nothing'; distinct from a + el) · also a + el before an infinitive 'on, upon' (al exir de Salón 'on leaving the Jalón'; = al salir) · al 'the other thing, the rest' in al feredes adelant 'the rest you will do later'
i: e/i — and (variant of e before some sounds) · also i — there, therein (adverb, Latin ibi, like French y; meted i las fedes, 'put your pledged faith into it')
tornado: tornar — returned (past participle; tornado es 'has returned', ser as perfect auxiliary; = tornado)
mandado: mandado — message, news, word (noun; from mandar 'to send, order') · also mandado — order, command (mandado de so señor 'the lord's command'); fazer mandado 'to send word' · also past part. 'granted, assigned' (el quinto que me avedes mandado 'the fifth you have granted me')
pesando: pesar — grieving, distressed (gerund; pesando va 'goes on grieving'; = pesando)
dan: dar — they give (present 3rd pl.; vagar non se dan 'they allow themselves no leisure'; = dan) · also dar — 'to pay (tribute)' (dan parias 'they pay tribute')
parias: paria — tribute paid by the Muslim taifa kingdoms to Castile (pl.)
tornando: tornar — turning (gerund; la cabeça tornando va 'he goes turning his head'; = tornando)
van: ir — they go (present 3rd pl.) · also ir + gerund 'keep going' (passando van 'they go on passing') · also ir + infinitive 'go to' (le van çercar 'they go to besiege him'; se van tornar 'they go back')
plogo: plazer — it pleased (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = plugo, modern plació)
mucho: mucho — much, greatly · also mucho — very, intensifying a predicate (mucho es mañana 'it is much too early, too soon')
sonrrisós: sonrreír + se — he smiled (sonrrisó + -s(e); = sonrrisóse, -se reduced to -s after a stressed vowel)
endurar: endurar — to endure, bear, hold back (infinitive; non lo pudo endurar 'could not bear it'; = aguantar)
he: aver — I have (1st sg. present; perfect auxiliary, = he, and the auxiliary of the split future, e.g. doblar vos he)
qui: qui — he who, whoever (old relative pronoun, Latin qui; = quien) · also qui — who? (interrogative; ¿qui los podrié contar? 'who could count them?'; = quién)
un: uno — a, one (apocopated masc. before a noun)
siempre: siempre — always, forever; por siempre 'for ever'
so: so/su — his, her, its (unstressed possessive sg.; so çervicio = su servicio); also seer — I am (1st sg. present; = soy; so ayrado, 'I am in [the king's] ira')
cras: cras — tomorrow (adverb, Latin cras; cras a la mañana 'tomorrow morning'; modern uses mañana)
mañana: mañana — morning (a la mañana 'in the morning'; otro dia mañana 'next morning'; = mañana) · also mañana — early, soon (adverb/predicate; mucho es mañana 'it is too soon (to take back a man in disgrace after only three weeks)'; = pronto, temprano)
penssemos: pensar — let us set about (present subjunctive 1st pl., exhortation; pensar de + inf.; = pensemos)
dent: dent — of it, thereof (de + ent, a form of ende 'thence'; non nos darán dent nada 'they will give us none of it'; = de ello)
corre: correr — it runs, flows (present 3rd sg.; = corre)
mont: Mont — mount, hill (Latin montem; = monte); Mont Mayor, the place Martín Muñoz held: Montemayor, a Portuguese town he governed for Alfonso VI, according to Pidal · also Mont Real — Monreal, name of the place above which the Cid's hill stands (Pidal: Monreal del Campo, on the Jiloca); see real
ovieron: aver — they had, they got (strong preterite of aver; = hubieron)
foron: seer — they were (preterite 3rd pl., variant of fueron; = fueron)
mandados: mandado — message, news, report (pl.; here the tidings that spread; = mandados)
partes: parte — part, quarter, direction (pl.); de todas partes 'from every quarter'
así: así — thus, so; así como 'as soon as'
mal: mal — harm, hurt, ruin · mal — evil, in the prayer's sense (por end es salvo de mal 'therefore he is saved from evil') · also mal — adverb 'sorely, ill' (por cuer le pesó mal 'it grieved him sorely at heart')
